meaning: A similarity_guard_group is a split-safety constraint only. It forces the original groups it links into the SAME train/validation/test partition. It does NOT claim the linked images are the same physical leaf. It does NOT overwrite, replace, or modify any authoritative leaf_id. It does NOT replace or modify any approved Tomato filename-family group key. Every image's original group_key and group_source are preserved unchanged in all manifests and reports -- a similarity_guard_group is an additional, separate column recorded alongside them, never a substitute for them.

guards.reason: M3B-3A visual inspection found the two images closely matching in leaf outline, lesion distribution, and background/lighting, despite carrying different authoritative leaf_ids (157.0 vs 164.0) in the upstream leaf-counting metadata. Not currently cross-split under the prior (pre-guard) allocation, both landed in train by coincidence, not by any enforced policy. Applied as a precautionary split-safety measure.

M3B-3A visual inspection found these two images the least visually similar of the three flagged clusters -- different curl/wilt stage, lesion shape, and leaf orientation -- plausibly two genuinely different leaves that pHash flagged on coarse structure/color rather than fine content. Different authoritative leaf_ids (207.0 vs 171.0). Not currently cross-split, both landed in train by coincidence. Applied uniformly with the other two guards as a low-cost, consistent, easily-auditable policy rather than a case-by-case judgment call, even though disclosure-only would also have been defensible for this specific pair.

M3B-3A visual inspection found these two images near-identical -- same distinctive scalloped leaf silhouette, same lesion position/color, same background, same small debris speck in the same position. Neither image has an authoritative leaf_id (both were originally unmatched in the M3A leaf-map join and resolved only via the M3B-2 filename-family rule as two separate singleton groups, since 'Leaf 8836' and 'Leaf 8837' are adjacent but different leaf numbers under the tlb:: grouping key). Under the prior (pre-guard) allocation this pair was ACTUALLY cross-split: Leaf8836 assigned to train, Leaf8837 assigned to validation -- a real, live near-duplicate leakage risk, not merely a hypothetical one. This guard is the mandatory case among the three.

constraints.no_cross_class_guards: Every guard's original_group_keys belong to images of a single class_name; no guard links groups across different classes.
constraints.no_overlapping_guards: No original_group_key appears in more than one guard_group_id in this file.
constraints.does_not_overwrite_authoritative_data: This file does not modify training/class_map.json, training/model_scope_v1.json, or training/tomato_grouping_policy_v1.json, and does not change any leaf_id or filename-family group_key recorded elsewhere.
